Thanks for the demo last week — the team found Redwood's routing and cost controls compelling. Specifically: 

- A controls matrix mapping safeguards for EU -> US processing (KV cache handling, model routing, and subprocessor list).
- A copy or redline of the proposed DPA annex we can circulate to legal.
- A short note describing KMS usage and key custody / rotation (we only need a 1–2 paragraph summary).

Timebox: can you provide these by EOD Thursday (May 16)? If there are items that require an NDA/secure transfer, let us know and we can arrange.

Best,
Marie Lemoine

Marie — thanks for the clear ask and for the time last week. We're happy to deliver a concise evidence pack. High level note up front: Redwood supports routing to EU-only or US-only inference pools, and when EU->US processing is required we provide documented safeguards (contractual commitments + technical controls) consistent with DPF standards published by the ACN.

Action plan:
- We'll attach a controls matrix that maps technical and contractual safeguards to each transfer vector (API, model training telemetry, logs).
- I'll attach a draft DPA annex with our suggested language; Karthik will review the legal redlines prior to sending final.
- Ben will provide the 2-paragraph KMS/key custody summary and a short diagram of network egress controls.

We will send the materials as attachments to this thread by EOD Thursday 16 May. If you prefer a secure drive link instead, confirm and we will post to the shared folder and notify you.

Quick clarification question for your privacy team: are you looking for evidence that processing only occurs in the US when requested (i.e., strict regional residency), or are you validating safeguards for one-off transfers originating in the EU to US endpoints? That will determine how we document routing fallback behavior vs. residency guarantees.

Thanks — Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Privacy & Trust Counsel
Redwood Inference
From: Marie Lemoine <marie.lemoine@medsupply.com>

Hi Olga — thanks for the quick reply. Good question: our default ask is that MedSupply can require EU-only processing for our EU controller data. However, we also need a documented path showing how Redwood handles ad hoc export (EU->US) when invoked by our application (e.g., for US-only downstream models). In other words: 1) residency contractual option, and 2) documented safeguards for exports where residency is not enforced.

Also, a follow-up: can you confirm whether Redwood's KV cache content is ever persisted to non-EU storage by default, and whether KV cache snapshots are included in backup/monitoring telemetry? Our security team wants to ensure no residual fragments remain outside the requested jurisdiction.

Appreciate it — Marie
From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: Marie Lemoine <marie.lemoine@medsupply.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 May 2029 14:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: detailed controls evidence for EU->US exports and DPF compatibility

Marie — attaching the evidence set below. Summary of key points inline, followed by attachments.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Residency option: Redwood supports explicit "region pinning" for controller-configured datasets. When pinning is enabled, requests are routed only to physical inference pools in the specified region; we provide contractual SLRs for processing locality in the DPA annex.
- Ad hoc export safeguards: when an export to US endpoints is requested, we document routing policy, fallbacks, and an audit trail. Exports are subject to encryption-in-transit, endpoint authentication, and per-request logging. We map those controls to DPF criteria in the attached matrix.
- KV cache handling: KV cache entries used for inference are stored in-memory on the serving host and are not persisted to cross-region backups by default. We do persist short-lived cache snapshots to encrypted storage for crash recovery, but those snapshots inherit the region placement policy of the hosting pool; we can disable snapshot persistence for datasets you mark as EU-resident. KV cache snapshots are rotated every 6 hours and deleted per the retention schedule (30 days default; can be reduced via contract).
- Key management: Redwood uses customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) via KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted customers may use Redwood-managed KMS with tenant isolation. Key rotation policy and HSM-backed signing details are included in the attached text file.

Attachments included: redwood_dpf_controls_matrix.xlsx (mapping to DPF control categories), dpa_annex_draft_medSupply.pdf (annotated draft annex with residency clauses), kms_key_lifecycle_overview.txt, network-egress-topology.png.

Next steps:
- Karthik and Ben will lead any follow-up technical Q&A with your infra/security SMEs.
- If MedSupply's legal wants to redline the DPA annex, please send to k.iyer@redwood.com and we'll reply with tracked changes within 3 business days.

If you'd like a short walkthrough (30 minutes) of the matrix and snapshot handling, we can schedule tomorrow morning CET.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Privacy & Trust Counsel
Redwood Inference
